subject: Prerequisite data modification for running CommonfactorGWAS

messages.author: be2e279c49e4b767
messages.subject: Prerequisite data modification for running CommonfactorGWAS
parts:
Hello,
 
We are using Genomic SEM's commonfactorGWAS to generate summary statistics with 7 trait components of Metabolic syndrome. Our aim is to generate a PRS score for Metabolic syndrome.
Some of the GWAS summary statistics used are presented in reference to the allele on the forward strand while others are in the reverse strand. Our questions are the following:
 
1- Should the summary statistics reported on the reverse strands be flipped to the forward strand before munging (i.e. ensure same direction across all files)?
 
2- Additionally, some of our traits are from the same cohort study. Is it okay to munge GWAS  summary statistics if some of the component traits are from the same study population/cohort?
 
3- Should the effect allele be arranged such that the allele shows increased risk?

Thanks you for your time!

Best regards,
Nada

messages.author: ac421cf36d1a4c37
messages.subject: Re: Prerequisite data modification for running CommonfactorGWAS
parts:
For standard sumstats, munge should take care of aligning to a common ref panel etc... 
Please be sure to consult the wiki and our papers (especially https://doi.org/10.1038/s41562-019-0566-x1).
One particular strength of Genomic SEM is that the sumstats can come from samples with varying and/or unknown degrees of overlap. However, traits that are directly computed as linear composites of other traits from the same sample that are in your analysis should not be included (i.e. you should not be able to predict one trait from the other traits with R2=100%), as this would introduce inappropriate dependencies in the data.
